review.reason: The frozen acceptance genuinely forces a correct record-read implementation and cannot be gamed. The tests build the real subject end-to-end: real TransformationService seed/refresh (load_subscriptions/load_contract_prices/load_transactions/refresh_publications), real create_app, real router, and a real ReportingService wired to a test-local DuckDB publication adapter that executes the reporting layer's own %s-parameterized SQL (the adapter only translates %s->?; it returns no canned rows). Expectations are derived from the existing list endpoints, and assert_resolves requires multiset equality plus per-row source_key == item_id, so constant results, ignored inputs, and subject mocks all fail. Equal-looking upcoming charges (distinct charge_id, identical visible name/date/amount) and the grid / grid_north / grid/north prefix-and-slash contract ids defeat first-row and equal-looking shortcuts, and the encoded-slash {item_id:path} round-trip forces the real HTTP/router path. The base-failure claim is verified correct: all imports resolve (build_oidc_provider/build_session_manager re-exported from packages.shared.auth; MockOidcIssuer.issue_token/http_client; IngestionConfigRepository carries SQLiteAuthControlPlaneMixin; RunMetadataRepository, AccountTransactionService, subscription_charge_id, DuckDBStore, PostgresReportingStore, running_postgres_container all exist); create_app accepts every keyword used; the record route and the four generated OpenAPI paths are absent on 9cf62cb, and the single-segment /reports/{extension_key} catch-all cannot match the multi-segment record path (404); generated openapi.json and api.d.ts exist so the contracts test fails on missing paths, not FileNotFoundError; the Postgres test is marked slow and deselected by addopts='-m not slow'; and the auth detail strings (X permission required., 401 Authentication required.) match middleware_authorization. Seed counts were traced against the anomaly/review/renewal logic and are correct: 240 first-occurrence anomalies (each 'Vendor NNN' is a distinct counterparty with |amount|>=50), 3 'Regular Grocer' rows are non-anomalies (stddev 0), 4 review, 4 renewal, 2 upcoming. Residual precision gaps (below) are refinements, not holes: none admits a wrong implementation, and none invalidates the red-on-base guarantee.
review.trivial_pass: Attacks attempted and why they fail. (1) Constant results / hardcoded rows: assert_resolves compares canon(rows) against list-endpoint-derived expected rows as a multiset and asserts every returned row's source_key == item_id, so a constant body cannot match 240 distinct anomaly keys, the 4 review/4 renewal/2 upcoming keys, or the per-identity component rows. (2) Ignored item_id (return full list / first row / equal-looking row): test_out_of_first_page_anomaly_is_selected_by_exact_key resolves a non-first page key to exactly one row; test_component_rows_belong_only_to_the_same_canonical_identity distinguishes review_grid/north_above_market_average {current_price 2,3} from review_grid_multiple_contracts_same_type {grid} and review_grid_north_multiple_contracts_same_type {grid_north}; test_equal_looking_upcoming_charges_resolve_to_distinct_rows requires two equal-looking charges to map to their own charge_id. (3) Mocking the subject: impossible to inject, because the test constructs ReportingService(ts, publication_store=store, access_mode=PUBLISHED) directly with the real class and its own adapter; the only substitution point (publication_store) is test-owned and executes real SQL. (4) Cross-type/split/prefix shortcuts: cross-type reads are 400/404, and malformed keys (anomaly_, review_grid, review__above_market_average, renewal_grid_not-a-date, upcoming_None_<date>, SQL-injection '...'||'1'='1', uppercase transaction_id) must never resolve; these block naive string-splitting and concatenated-SQL lookups. (5) Warehouse fallback in PUBLISHED: a published row still resolves after the warehouse drops it, a warehouse-only row is 404, and a dropped published relation is 503, so a lazy get_*() fallback is caught. Remaining weakness (not a trivial pass, a mechanism gap): the intent's 'exact parameterized lookup before pagination/limits' is not independently enforced - a correct-but-unparameterized Python list-and-filter over the published store would satisfy every positive test, including the Postgres integration test, because none asserts the lookup used a single %s-parameterized WHERE rather than fetch-then-filter.
checks: BASE-FAILURE CORRECTNESS (verified, no revision needed): every non-slow test fails on 9cf62cb at a positive record read (404 from the absent route) or at the missing OpenAPI paths, never at collection/import/fixture. Verified: all test imports resolve; create_app accepts the keyword args (service, transformation_service, reporting_service, config_repository, auth_store, identity_mode, session_manager, oidc_provider); the record path /reports/<segment>/records/<item_id> matches no base route (the /reports/{extension_key} catch-all is single-segment, so the multi-segment path 404s); generated openapi.json and api.d.ts exist; the Postgres test is deselected via slow marker + addopts.

SEED COUNTS ARE CORRECT: 240 anomalies (each 'Vendor NNN' is a distinct counterparty, tx_count=1, |amount|>=50 => first_occurrence), 'Regular Grocer' rows excluded (stddev=0), 4 contract_review (grid/north above_market_average {2,3}, grid/north multiple {1}, grid multiple {1}, grid_north multiple {1}), 4 contract_renewal (grid/north @d10 {1,2}, grid/north @d20 {3}, grid @d10, grid_north @d20), 2 upcoming (same weekly occurrence, distinct charge_id).

GAP (partial-NULL under-specified): test_partially_null_identity_cannot_prove_absence accepts intact.status_code in (200, 503). The outcome implies an intact row should still resolve (200) while only the NULLed and unknown keys are 503, but the frozen test does not pin 200 for the intact row, so an implementation that globally 503s whenever any row has NULL identity would also pass. Tighten to assert intact_id == 200 (and its rows equal expected) if the intent means 'absence cannot be proven only for the affected keys'.

GAP (no-leak assertion is a token blacklist, not exact shape): assert_not_resolved checks 'detail' in body, 'rows' not in body, and a fixed forbidden token set (SOURCE_NAMES + other charge_ids) absent from the raw text. It does not require set(body) == {'detail'}, and SOURCE_NAMES does not include the contract ids ('grid', 'grid_north', 'grid/north'), reasons, dates, or amounts, so a failure body that leaks e.g. {'detail': ..., 'contract_id': 'grid'} would pass. The auth test's _assert_denied does enforce set(body) == {'detail'}, but the main record test does not. Consider asserting set(body) == {'detail'} in assert_not_resolved to fully enforce 'JSON {detail} without source-data leakage'.

GAP (mechanism not enforced): the intent's 'exact parameterized lookup before pagination/limits' is only enforced semantically (exact key, not first/equal-looking) via the equal-looking and out-of-first-page tests; a correct-but-unparameterized Python list-and-filter would pass all positive tests including Postgres. The Postgres integration test exercises the real %s fetchall_dicts only if the implementation itself chooses parameterized SQL; it does not reject a fetch-then-filter implementation.

GAP (OpenAPI schema check is shallow): _schema_refs only verifies the row-model $ref NAME is reachable anywhere in the 200 response schema, not that rows is array[RowModel] nor the {item_id, rows} response shape; a stray unrelated $ref to e.g. TransactionAnomaliesRow would satisfy it. It also does not document 404/503 error schemas. The generated['paths'][path] == live['paths'][path] equality is the real gate and is fine.

GAP (200 body keys not asserted exact): get_rows asserts body['item_id'] == item_id and body['rows'] non-empty list, but not set(body) == {'item_id', 'rows'}. FastAPI response_model would filter extra fields, so this is minor, but the test itself does not pin the shape.

NO TRIVIAL PASS FOUND: constant/hardcoded results, ignored item_id, first/equal-looking row, subject mock, and cross-type/prefix/split shortcuts are each defeated by the assertions above; the only real limitation is the unparameterized-lookup mechanism gap (noted) which preserves correctness but not the intent's efficiency/mechanism requirement.
